ai_diagnosis: DHCP pool exhausted – no available addresses
human_notes: Diagnosis confirmed via lab testing; cleared stale bindings to restore service.

ai_diagnosis: ACL permit any any placed before deny rule
human_notes: Verified in Packet Tracer – resequencing the ACL resolved guest access to internal server.
Confirmed – PC had gateway set to 192.168.1.100 instead of 192.168.1.1.

ai_diagnosis: Missing DNS server configuration on client
human_notes: Correct root cause; nslookup was querying 127.0.0.1 instead of 10.0.0.53.

ai_diagnosis: Missing ip nat inside/outside on interfaces
human_notes: Lab verification confirmed no NAT translations were being created until interface designations were added.

AI identified pool exhaustion correctly but fix_steps only suggested clearing all bindings. Edited to include expanding the pool subnet from /26 to /24 and adding excluded-address range for infrastructure IPs, which is the sustainable long-term fix.

ai_diagnosis: NAT access-list not matching inside traffic
human_notes: AI diagnosed an ACL issue with NAT but the real problem was the missing 'ip nat inside' on GigabitEthernet0/1. Corrected root_cause and fix_steps to add the interface designation instead of modifying the NAT ACL.
Confirmed by running 'show interfaces trunk' on both switches – VLAN 30 was absent from the allowed list.
Verified – Router C was not advertising 10.0.30.0/24. Adding the network statement restored reachability.
Diagnosis confirmed; client was configured with no DNS server at all. Adding 8.8.8.8 resolved browsing.

ai_diagnosis: OSPF area mismatch between Router A and Router C
human_notes: AI claimed an area mismatch was preventing adjacency, but 'show ip ospf interface' confirmed both interfaces were in Area 0. The actual issue was a missing 'network 10.0.30.0 0.0.0.255 area 0' statement on Router C – the adjacency was up but the LAN subnet was simply not advertised.

ai_diagnosis: Client NIC driver incompatible with WPA2
human_notes: AI assumed a driver-level incompatibility because the laptop failed to associate. However, a second known-good laptop also failed, ruling out client-side issues. The access point had the wrong pre-shared key configured; correcting the PSK immediately resolved association for all clients.

AI blamed Spanning Tree Protocol for blocking the trunk, but 'show spanning-tree vlan 30' showed the port in forwarding state. Corrected to 'Missing VLAN 30 on trunk allowed list' – the trunk was simply not carrying VLAN 30 traffic because it was never added via switchport trunk allowed vlan.

ai_diagnosis: ACL deny rule applied to wrong interface
human_notes: Confirmed the ACL was on the correct interface but the rule ordering was wrong. The permit any any at sequence 10 was matching before the deny, effectively bypassing all filtering.

ai_diagnosis: Incorrect default gateway on end host
human_notes: Verified – PC had no default gateway configured. Adding 192.168.1.1 as the gateway restored external connectivity.
